newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq and Russia to set up oil company - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq and Russia to set up oil company - paper.

text.p: Iraq and Russia have taken fresh steps to establish a joint Iraqi-Russian oil drilling company, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said on Saturday.
The paper quoted the director-general of the state-run oil drilling company, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, as saying the two sides had agreed to set up the firm last March.
"The general tasks of the company and its interior structure have been specified and members of its board of directors from both sides have been appointed," Abdulkarim said.
The paper gave no further details.
Iraq and Russia signed on March 21 an oil deal under which Moscow was expected to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in Iraq's southern Qurna oilfield.

The 23-year contract includes a plan under which Russia is expected to lift about 600,000 barrels per day (bpd). According to experts, this will consume half of Qurna's proven reserves in 23 years at the end of which the Russians are obliged to hand it back to Iraq.

The international trade curbs imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait place a blanket ban on its oil exports and investments in the country. The United Nations has allowed Iraq to pump $2 billion worth of oil over six months on humanitarian grounds.
"Both sides are keen to speed up measures of establishing the Iraqi-Russian joint company which consists of two Russian companies and the Iraqi oil drilling company," Abdulkarim said.
